probe_meta.label: dense-G (controlled retrieval-mechanism swap of Probe G)

response_text:
1. (Currently amended) A method of treating a brain, comprising: inserting an elongated device into the brain to create a path; radially expanding the device to create a working channel along the path; and introducing a medical element into the working channel to perform a medical procedure on the brain, __wherein the elongated device is inserted into the brain and radially expanded without inserting the elongated device between tissue layers within the brain__.

2. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the medical element is an instrument.

3. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the medical element is a medicament.

4. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, further comprising creating an opening in a cranium, and inserting the elongated device through the opening.

5. (Cancelled)

6. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, further comprising radially contracting and removing the device from the brain.

7. (Currently amended) A method of treating a tissue, comprising: placing an elongated device into the tissue to create a path; radially expanding the device against the tissue to radially displace the tissue along the path; radially reinforcing the device against the tissue; and introducing a medical element through the device to perform a medical procedure on the tissue, __wherein the elongated device is placed into the tissue and radially expanded without inserting the elongated device between tissue layers__.

8. (Currently amended) The method of claim 7, wherein the medical element is an instrument.

9. (Currently amended) The method of claim 7, wherein the medical element is a medicament.

10. (Cancelled)

11. (Currently amended) The method of claim 7, further comprising radially contracting and removing the device from the tissue.

12. (Currently amended) The method of claim 7, further comprising treating the tissue in contact with the device with a haemostatic compound to reduce bleeding.

13. (Cancelled)

14. (Cancelled)

15. (Original) The method of claim 13, wherein the medical element is a medicament.

16. (Cancelled)

17. (Original) The method of claim 13, fu rther comprising treating the tissue in contact with the device with a haemostatic compound to reduce bleeding.
